questions.question: According to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, what was the total number of recognized startups in India as of March 31, 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2.23 lakh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** announced that the total number of recognized startups under the **Startup India** initiative has surpassed **2.23 lakh** as of the end of **FY26**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **2.23 lakh**: This is the cumulative total of startups recognized by the Centre since the launch of the initiative in **2016** until **March 31, 2026**.
 
• **55,200**: This figure represents the record number of startups recognized in the single financial year of **2025-26** alone, the highest since the scheme's inception.
 
• **1.07 lakh**: Nearly 48% of the total recognized startups have at least **one woman director or partner**, showcasing rising female entrepreneurship.
 
• **38,600**: This is the number of startups currently onboarded on the **Government e-Marketplace (GeM)** platform to facilitate public procurement.
 
• The growth in startup recognition in **FY26** was **51.6%** year-on-year compared to the previous financial year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Employment**: The startup ecosystem has collectively generated over **23.36 lakh direct jobs** as of March 31, 2026, with **4.99 lakh** jobs created in FY26 alone.
 
• **Leading States**: **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, and Gujarat** have emerged as the primary hubs for startup numbers and job creation.
 
• **Funding Support**: Under the **Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS)**, over **₹7,000 crore** has been disbursed, and a new **Fund of Funds 2.0** with a **₹10,000 crore** corpus has been launched.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The **Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups** saw its guarantee cover per borrower double to **₹20 crore**.
 
• Innovation is rising, as evidenced by **patent filings** increasing from 2,850 in FY25 to more than **4,480 in FY26**.
 
• The total order value for startups on the **GeM portal** rose to over **₹19,190 crore** in FY26.

questions.question: What was the annual rate of inflation (Year-on-Year) based on the All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for the month of March 2026?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.88%**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Commerce & Industry** released the **Wholesale Price Index (WPI)** data for **March 2026**, showing an annual inflation rate of **3.88%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **March 2026 WPI Inflation:** The annual rate of inflation (Y-o-Y) for all commodities stood at **3.88%** (provisional), up from previous months.
 
• **Reasons for Increase:** The rise in inflation was primarily driven by higher prices in **crude petroleum & natural gas**, **non-food articles**, **basic metals**, and **food articles**.
 
• **Comparison with January and February:** The inflation rate for **January 2026** was finalized at **1.68%**, while the provisional rate for **February 2026** was **2.13%**.
 
• **Primary Articles:** This major group saw a significantly higher annual inflation rate of **6.36%** in March 2026.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **WPI Food Index:** The inflation rate for the **Food Index** remained constant at **1.85%** in March 2026 compared to February 2026.
 
• **MoM Change:** The month-over-month (M-o-M) change in WPI for March 2026 was **1.64%** compared to February 2026.
 
• **Crude Petroleum:** Crude petroleum saw a massive surge in prices with an annual inflation rate of **51.57%** and a monthly increase of **49.10%** in March 2026.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Base Year:** The current WPI series in India uses **2011-12** as the base year.
 
• **Releasing Authority:** The index is released monthly by the **DPIIT** (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) on the 14th of every month.
 
• **Response Rate:** The provisional WPI for March 2026 was compiled with a weighted response rate of **77.8%**.

questions.question: India is ranked _______ in the World Happiness Report published in March 2025.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**118th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **World Happiness Report 2025**, published in **March 2025**, **India ranked 118th** among **147 countries**.
 
• The report is published annually by the **Wellbeing Research Centre at the University of Oxford**, in partnership with **Gallup**, the **UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**, and the **editorial board of the World Happiness Report**.
 
• The rankings are based on people's self-assessed life evaluations and factors such as **GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption**.
 
• **Finland** retained the **1st position** for the **eighth consecutive year** in the 2025 report.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3 – 118th**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Top 5 Countries in the World Happiness Report 2025:**

 
 
• 1. Finland
 
• 2. Denmark
 
• 3. Iceland
 
• 4. Sweden
 
• 5. Netherlands
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Report:**
 
 
• It measures the happiness and well-being of people across countries using survey data and socio-economic indicators.
 
 
 
• **Release:**
 
 
• The report is released annually on or around the **International Day of Happiness (20 March)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Rank (World Happiness Report 2025):** **118th**.
 
• **Total Countries Ranked:** **147**.
 
• **Top-ranked Country:** **Finland** (8th consecutive year).
 
• **Published By:** Wellbeing Research Centre, University of Oxford, in partnership with Gallup, SDSN, and the World Happiness Report editorial board.
 
• **Released:** March 2025 (around 20 March – International Day of Happiness).

questions.question: India’s rank in the Responsible Nation Index 2026 is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's rank in the Responsible Nation Index 2026** is **16th**, as per the most recent global survey conducted for evaluating responsible governance and sustainability measures across nations.
 
• The **Responsible Nation Index** is a globally recognized ranking that assesses countries based on their contributions to **sustainability, ethical governance, and global cooperation**.
 
• India's improvement in the index reflects its growing efforts toward **sustainable development goals (SDGs)**, focusing on areas like climate change, renewable energy, and gender equality.
 
• In previous editions of the Responsible Nation Index, India ranked slightly lower, which indicates an upward trajectory in terms of its global responsibilities and contributions.
 
• Countries that ranked higher than India include developed nations like **Norway, Finland, and Sweden**, which consistently perform well in parameters such as environmental sustainability and social equity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Responsible Nation Index (RNI):**

 
 
• The Responsible Nation Index is a benchmark that evaluates the performance of countries on various global issues, including **sustainability, human rights, climate action, economic equality, and global cooperation**.
 
• The rankings are based on data from global organizations such as the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**, **World Bank**, and other credible sources.
 
 
 
• **India's Focus Areas for Improvement:**
 
 
• **Climate Change:** India has committed to **reducing its carbon emissions intensity by 45%** by 2030, as part of its updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
 
• **Renewable Energy:** India is one of the leading countries in renewable energy, with ambitious targets to achieve **500 GW of renewable energy capacity** by 2030.
 
 
 
• **Top Performing Nations in the Index:**
 
 
• **Norway:** Ranked 1st for its exceptional contributions to **social welfare, climate action, and inclusive governance**.
 
• **Sweden:** Known for its commitment to **clean energy and sustainability**, consistently ranks among the top performers.
 
 
 
• **Relevant Global Indices:**
 
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** India ranks 132nd (2022) and is improving steadily in areas like **healthcare, education, and standard of living**.
 
• **Global Climate Risk Index:** India faces challenges due to its vulnerability to **climate change and natural disasters**, yet its proactive measures have been acknowledged globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Progress:**

 
 
• India's rank at **16th** reflects its growing global presence in terms of sustainable and inclusive growth.
 
• Efforts like the **National Solar Mission** and **Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana** have contributed to improving India's standing in global indices.
 
 
 
• **Global Cooperation:**
 
 
• India is actively participating in global initiatives such as the **Paris Agreement**, **International Solar Alliance (ISA)**, and **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.

questions.question: Which organisation releases the Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNESCO**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• The **Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report** is an annual publication released by the **United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).** 

• The GEM Report was first published in **2016** and serves as a continuation of the earlier **Education for All Global Monitoring Reports**. 

• The primary objective of the GEM Report is to **monitor the progress of education systems** globally and assess the implementation of **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4)**, which aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education. 

• The report provides a comprehensive analysis of global education trends, policies, and challenges, covering aspects like **access, equity, quality, and financing of education**. 

• Each annual report has a **specific theme**. For instance, the 2023 GEM Report focuses on **technology and education**, addressing how digital tools can support learning and the challenges of digital divides. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **UNESCO:** 
 

• **UNESCO** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** established in **1945** with its headquarters in **Paris, France**. 

• Its mission is to promote **international collaboration in education, science, culture, and communication** to contribute to peace and security. 

• UNESCO is responsible for monitoring progress toward **SDG 4** of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, which focuses on education. 

• It works in areas such as **literacy, teacher training, gender equality in education, and digital education**. 
 
 

• **Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4):** 
 

• SDG 4 is one of the 17 goals under the **United Nations 2030 Agenda**. 

• Its main aim is to **“Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all.”** 

• The goal focuses on aspects like **universal primary and secondary education**, eliminating gender disparities, improving literacy rates, and ensuring quality education. 
 
 

• **Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report Themes:** 
 

• Each year, the GEM Report focuses on a unique theme related to education. Examples of past themes include: 
 

• **2020:** Inclusion and Education: All Means All. 

• **2021:** Non-state actors in education. 

• **2023:** Technology and education. 
 
 

• The themes address emerging challenges, including **equity, financing, and the role of technology** in education. 
 
 

• **Reports and Indices by Other Organizations:** 
 

• **UNICEF:** Publishes reports like the **State of the World’s Children Report**, focusing on child welfare and education. 

• **UNDP:** Produces the **Human Development Report**, which includes the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, analyzing education, health, and standard of living. 

• **World Bank:** Publishes reports like the **World Development Report**, which also covers education and economic development. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Relevance of GEM Report:** 
 

• The GEM Report is a critical resource for policymakers and educators as it provides evidence-based insights and recommendations. 

• It highlights **key challenges** such as disparities in access to education, the impact of poverty, and technological integration in learning. 
 
 

• **Global Impact:** 
 

• The report is widely cited and used by governments, NGOs, and international organizations to shape policies and initiatives aimed at improving global education systems. 

• It has been instrumental in promoting **data-driven decision-making** in the field of education. 
 
 
 
5d:T

questions.question: In 2025, which United Nations body released the World Urbanization Prospects report using the Degree of Urbanization methodology?

options.text: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Urbanization Prospects (WUP)** is a flagship publication produced by the **Population Division** of the **United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**.
 
• The **2025 Revision** of this report represents a landmark shift as it is the first edition to fully implement the **Degree of Urbanization (DegUrba)** methodology for global comparative analysis.
 
• The **Degree of Urbanization** is a hierarchical classification that distinguishes the entire territory of a country into three main types of areas: **Cities**, **Towns and semi-dense areas**, and **Rural areas**.
 
• This methodology was formally endorsed by the **United Nations Statistical Commission** in **March 2020** during its **51st session** to harmonize the diverse and often incomparable national definitions of "urban" and "rural" areas.
 
• By using **population density** and **grid-based data** (typically **1 km² cells**), **UN DESA** aims to provide more consistent and accurate data on global urban trends, which is vital for international comparisons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)**: Established in **1948** and headquartered in **New York**, **USA**, it acts as a vital interface between global policies and national action. The **Population Division** within **UN DESA** provides the international community with up-to-date estimates and projections of population **age**, **location**, and **growth**.
 
• **World Urbanization Prospects (WUP)**: This series has been published since **1988**. It provides a comprehensive set of estimates and projections of the **urban** and **rural** populations of all countries in the world and of their major **urban agglomerations**.
 
• **UN-Habitat**: Based in **Nairobi**, **Kenya**, the **United Nations Human Settlements Programme** focuses on sustainable **urban development** and the implementation of the **New Urban Agenda**. While they collaborate on data, the primary statistical responsibility for the **WUP** report lies with **UN DESA**.
 
• **Global Urbanization Trends**: According to previous reports, **55%** of the world’s population lived in urban areas in **2018**, a figure that is projected to increase to **68%** by the year **2050**. Most of this growth is expected to take place in **Asia** and **Africa**.
 
• **Statistical Commission**: This is the highest body of the global statistical system, bringing together Chief Statisticians from **Member States**. It oversees the work of the **United Nations Statistics Division (UNSD)** and ensures that international standards like the **Degree of Urbanization** are adopted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of DegUrba**: Before the adoption of this methodology, countries used their own criteria (such as **administrative boundaries**, **population size**, or **economic functions**) to define urban areas, making it difficult to compare a city in **India** with a city in **France** or **Brazil**.
 
• **SDG Monitoring**: The use of standardized urbanization data by **UN DESA** is crucial for monitoring **Sustainable Development Goal 11 (SDG 11)**, which seeks to make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient, and sustainable by **2030**.
 
• **Leading Contributors to Growth**: It is estimated that just three countries—**India**, **China**, and **Nigeria**—will account for **35%** of the total growth in the world’s urban population between **2018** and **2050**. **India** is projected to add **416 million** urban dwellers.
 
• **Data Sources**: The report relies on **national census** data, **satellite imagery**, and **geospatial information** to refine the application of the **Degree of Urbanization** methodology across different **countries** and **continents**.

questions.question: The Logistics Performance Index measures effectiveness of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trade & Logistics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Logistics Performance Index (LPI) is a benchmarking tool created by the World Bank to measure the efficiency and performance of logistics and trade systems globally.
 
• It evaluates countries based on six key dimensions: customs performance, infrastructure quality, ease of arranging shipments, competence and quality of logistics services, tracking and tracing capabilities, and timeliness of shipments.
 
• The LPI helps identify challenges and opportunities in the logistics sector, enabling policymakers and stakeholders to improve trade facilitation and supply chain efficiency.
 
• It is published every two years and includes both qualitative and quantitative assessments based on surveys of logistics professionals.
 
• The index is crucial in analyzing the impact of effective logistics on international trade, economic growth, and global competitiveness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Systems:**

 
 
• Financial systems refer to a set of institutions, markets, instruments, and regulatory frameworks that facilitate the flow of funds and allocation of resources in an economy.
 
• They include banks, capital markets, insurance companies, pension funds, and other financial intermediaries.
 
• While financial systems play a vital role in economic growth, they are not directly related to logistics performance.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture:**
 
 
• Agriculture involves the cultivation of crops and livestock for food, fiber, and other products essential for human sustenance.
 
• Although logistics plays a role in agriculture (e.g., transportation of goods), the Logistics Performance Index is not specifically designed to measure agricultural efficiency or productivity.
 
 
 
• **Cybersecurity:**
 
 
• Cybersecurity involves protecting systems, networks, and data from digital attacks, theft, or damage.
 
• It is primarily concerned with safeguarding information technology infrastructure and does not relate to the measurement of logistics performance.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme - Trade & Logistics:**
 
 
• The effectiveness of logistics is a critical component of international trade, impacting supply chain efficiency, cost reduction, and timely delivery of goods.
 
• Improved logistics systems foster better integration into global value chains and enhance the competitiveness of economies.
 
• Trade facilitation measures, including infrastructure development and efficient customs processes, are essential for improving logistics performance.

questions.question: What was India’s global rank in mental health and well-being for young adults (aged 18–34) according to the Global Mind Health 2025 report?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Global Firepower Index** ranks countries based on their military strength by analyzing more than **60 individual factors**, including logistics, geography, and natural resources, apart from conventional military assets.
 
• These factors ensure a comprehensive assessment of a country's ability to sustain military operations beyond just troop strength or nuclear capabilities. *This makes the methodology highly detailed and multidimensional.*
 
• The methodology also includes variables such as **defense budgets, manpower availability, industrial capacity, and geographic positioning**, which play a critical role in determining a country's military potential. *Hence, the correct statement is option 3.*
 
• Statements like "Only troop strength is assessed" and "Rankings rely solely on nuclear strength" are incorrect because the index uses a multidimensional approach rather than focusing on a single factor.
 
• Countries are not ranked alphabetically by region, as the ranking is based on the strength scores derived from the analysis of various factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Firepower Index:**

 
 
• The **Global Firepower Index** is an annual ranking that evaluates the military strength of countries worldwide using a **unique PowerIndex score**.
 
• The score is calculated using a wide range of parameters such as **manpower, equipment, financials, and geography**. A lower score indicates higher military strength.
 
• It is widely regarded as one of the most comprehensive assessments of military strength globally.
 
 
 
• **Factors Included in the Assessment:**
 
 
• **Manpower:** Includes active personnel, reserve forces, and paramilitary forces.
 
• **Military Equipment:** Includes tanks, aircraft, naval assets, and missile systems.
 
• **Geography:** Considers factors like landmass, coastline length, and access to key waterways.
 
• **Logistics:** Evaluates resources like fuel, transportation, and industrial capacity.
 
• **Finance:** Takes into account the defense budget, purchasing power parity, and financial health of the country.
 
 
 
• **Weightage and Exemptions:**
 
 
• Some factors like nuclear stockpiles are accounted for but are not given excessive weight to maintain fairness for non-nuclear countries.
 
• Geopolitical considerations, such as alliances (e.g., NATO), are also factored in but do not dominate the rankings.
 
 
 
• **Top-Ranked Countries:**
 
 
• The **United States** consistently ranks first due to its vast military budget, advanced technology, and significant global presence.
 
• Other leading countries include **Russia, China, and India**, which possess considerable manpower, military hardware, and strategic geographical advantages.
 
 
 
• **Applications and Importance:**
 
 
• The index is used by policymakers, analysts, and researchers to understand global military dynamics and trends.
 
• It highlights **areas of strength and vulnerability** for individual countries, aiding in defense planning and strategy formulation.

questions.question: Which country was ranked highest for gender equality in the Global Gender Gap Report, 2025, released by the World Economic Forum in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iceland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iceland** ranked the highest in the **Global Gender Gap Report 2025**, continuing its legacy as the most gender-equal nation globally.
 
• Iceland has been consistently performing well in gender equality metrics such as **economic participation, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment**.
 
• The nation has achieved nearly **91.2%** of gender parity, according to the World Economic Forum's latest report.
 
• Iceland’s success is attributed to progressive policies like **mandatory parental leave for both genders, equal pay laws, and strong representation of women in politics and business**.
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Report**, published by the **World Economic Forum**, evaluates gender equality across nations using various indices and is considered a crucial tool for assessing global progress.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Global Gender Gap Report:**

 
 
• The **Global Gender Gap Report** was first introduced by the **World Economic Forum** in **2006**.
 
• It measures gender equality across four dimensions: **Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment**.
 
• The report ranks countries based on their performance in closing the gender gap, with **0 representing absolute inequality** and **1 representing absolute equality**.
 
• It serves as a crucial benchmark for policymakers to address gender disparities globally.
 
 
 
• **Iceland’s Gender Equality Initiatives:**
 
 
• Iceland has a **mandatory parental leave policy**, where both parents are entitled to three months of leave, ensuring shared parenting responsibilities.
 
• The country passed **equal pay legislation in 2018**, requiring companies to prove they pay men and women equally.
 
• Women in Iceland hold significant political representation, with over **40% of parliamentary seats** occupied by women.
 
• Public protests, such as the **1975 Women’s Strike**, played a critical role in shaping Iceland’s gender equality policies.
 
 
 
• **Other High-Ranking Countries:**
 
 
• **Norway:** Known for its robust policies on gender equality, including strong parental leave and workplace equality programs.
 
• **Sweden:** A pioneer in gender-neutral policies and equal representation in government and corporate sectors.
 
• **Germany:** Despite significant advancements, Germany trails behind Nordic countries in achieving full gender parity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Gender Equality:**
 
 
• Gender equality is essential for achieving **sustainable development** and ensuring social justice.
 
• It contributes to higher economic productivity and fosters a more inclusive society.
 
• Eliminating gender disparities is crucial for achieving global goals like the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 5**, which focuses on gender equality.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Trends:** Iceland has been ranked **first** in the Global Gender Gap Report for more than a decade, showcasing its consistent commitment to gender equality.
 
• **Impact of Policies:** Iceland’s proactive measures, such as equal pay laws and gender quotas, have significantly influenced its performance.
 
• **Global Challenges:** Despite progress in some countries, global gender parity is projected to take over **130 years** to achieve, highlighting the need for accelerated efforts.

questions.question: According to the World Happiness Report, 2025, released in March 2025, which of the following countries ranked as the happiest country in the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Finland**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **World Happiness Report 2025**, released in March 2025, ranked **Finland as the happiest country in the world** for the sixth consecutive year.
 
• The rankings in the report are based on various indicators, including **GDP per capita, social support, life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption.**
 
• Finland consistently scores high due to its **strong social safety nets, excellent education and healthcare systems, low levels of corruption, and a high degree of personal and societal trust.**
 
• Other countries in the top five for 2025 include **Denmark, Switzerland, Iceland, and the Netherlands**, showcasing the dominance of Nordic and European nations in happiness rankings.
 
• Finland’s emphasis on **work-life balance, free education, environmental sustainability, and social equality** significantly contributes to its top position.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Happiness Report:**

 
 
• The report is an annual publication by the **Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)** of the United Nations.
 
• It evaluates 150+ countries based on a combination of **survey data from the Gallup World Poll** and other key indicators.
 
• The report’s goal is to provide insights into well-being and happiness levels globally, encouraging policymakers to prioritize happiness in development initiatives.
 
 
 
• **Finland’s Strengths:**
 
 
• **Social Support:** Finland has a robust welfare system that ensures citizens have access to healthcare, education, and unemployment benefits.
 
• **Education:** Finland’s education system is renowned for being free and accessible, focusing on equality and innovation.
 
• **Environmental Focus:** The country is known for its commitment to sustainability, clean energy, and preserving its abundant natural resources.
 
• **Trust and Transparency:** Finland consistently ranks as one of the least corrupt countries, fostering trust in government and institutions.
 
 
 
• **Other Countries:**
 
 
• **Denmark:** Known for its high levels of social equality, trust in government, and emphasis on work-life balance.
 
• **Switzerland:** Excels in healthcare, economic stability, and individual freedoms.
 
• **Iceland:** Praised for its gender equality, clean energy initiatives, and strong community ties.
 
• **Netherlands:** Offers a blend of economic prosperity, high-quality healthcare, and a progressive social structure.
 
 
 
• **Important Metrics in the Report:**
 
 
• **GDP per Capita:** Economic output per person, reflecting material well-being.
 
• **Social Support:** Measures the availability of assistance in times of need.
 
• **Healthy Life Expectancy:** Indicates the average number of years a person can expect to live in good health.
 
• **Freedom to Make Life Choices:** Reflects individuals’ perceived freedom to make decisions about their lives.
 
• **Generosity:** Based on donations to charities and community support.
 
• **Perceptions of Corruption:** Evaluates public trust in institutions and governance.

questions.question: World Social Security Report is released by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The World Social Security Report is published by the International Labour Organization (ILO).
 
• The ILO is a specialized agency of the United Nations established in 1919.
 
• Its headquarters is located in Geneva, Switzerland.
 
• **The report provides global data and analysis on:**
 
 
• Social protection coverage
 
• Social security systems
 
• Public expenditure on social protection
 
 
 
• It evaluates progress toward Universal Social Protection (USP).
 
• The report highlights gaps in coverage across regions and income groups.
 
• It examines pensions, unemployment benefits, healthcare access, maternity protection, and child benefits.
 
• The ILO uses data from governments and international statistical sources.
 
• The World Bank publishes reports like the World Development Report, but not the World Social Security Report.
 
• UN Women and the UN Human Rights Commission do not release this report.
 
• ***Therefore, the World Social Security Report is released by the International Labour Organization (ILO).***

questions.question: What is the score range for a Gram Panchayat to be classified as a 'Front Runner' under the Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**75 to below 90**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Panchayati Raj** released the **Panchayat Advancement Index (PAI) 2.0 Report** for the FY 2023–24 on **National Panchayati Raj Day**, celebrated on **24th April 2026**.

__
 
• Based on their composite PAI scores, Gram Panchayats are classified into five performance categories to enable meaningful benchmarking and healthy competition.
 
• **Front Runner (A)**: Gram Panchayats scoring from **75 to below 90** fall under this category. Hence, the correct answer is 75 to below 90.
 
• **Achiever (A+)**: Gram Panchayats scoring **90 and above**.
 
• **Performer (B)**: Gram Panchayats scoring from **60 to below 75**.
 
• **Aspirant (C)**: Gram Panchayats scoring from **40 to below 60**.
 
• **Beginner (D)**: Gram Panchayats scoring **below 40**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Indicators Framework**: PAI 2.0 evaluates Gram Panchayats against **150 indicators** and **230 data points** spanning nine thematic areas under the Localization of Sustainable Development Goals (LSDGs).
 
• **Top-performing Themes**: The highest outcomes were recorded under the themes of **Poverty Free and Enhanced Livelihoods** (3,313 GPs achieved A+ grade) and **Healthy Panchayats** (1,015 GPs attained A+ grade).

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The report revealed that a total of **3,635 Gram Panchayats** fall under the **Front Runner** category nationwide.
 
• **West Bengal** has not on-boarded in the exercise of PAI 2.0.

questions.question: Which report is specifically focused on global military expenditure?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 

• **SIPRI Yearbook** is an annual publication by the **Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI)**, which provides comprehensive data and analysis on **global military expenditure**, arms trade, and disarmament activities. 

• The Yearbook covers topics such as **military spending, arms production, international security, and arms control agreements**, making it the most authoritative source for military expenditure data globally. 

• It is widely regarded for its **transparent methodologies** and serves as a critical resource for researchers, policymakers, and international organizations studying global peace and security trends. 

• The SIPRI Yearbook includes detailed information on **worldwide trends in military spending**, highlighting the countries with the highest defense budgets, arms transfers, and nuclear weapons developments. 

•
